timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I'm here at Bethlehem.
Mayor John Fowell-Han, who's also candidate for US Congress next year.
What did you think of the event today?
I was excited.
It's always exciting when the President of the United States comes to visit the area.
And I think it was a great opportunity for us to hear him and what he's focused on
down in Washington, you see, which was clearly trying to get lower that our unemployment rate,
trying to get people back to work, trying to get this economy, you know, moving forward
and jump-started in a more rapid fashion.
And I was encouraged to hear some of the progress that's been made.
I think we all recognize that we didn't get here, you know, overnight.
And it's not going to be fixed overnight.
And I think the President is doing his best to roll up his sleeves and trying to put some
piles.
He's in place that are going to drive private sector investment that are going to stimulate
the job growth and economic investment.
And as he said, you know, to use his term, I think it's good when it's, you know, get
people, Americans back to work, building things that, building the things that America needs.
And so I was encouraged by what I heard.
And I think equally important is he was here to listen.
And I think he heard some things here that he will be able to take back to Washington,
DC and work with his cadets to try to, you know, come up with even further policies
system like the economy.
So, you know, I think it was great that he was here because, you know, Lehigh Valley
represents an area that's kind of really very much of a microcosm of the United States.
And mirrors a lot of the rest of this country.
It's got urban areas.
It's got three principal cities in Allentown, Betham, and Eastern.
It's got the suburbs and it's got some rural areas.
So in that sense, it's got a little bit of everything here in the land of Allian, and
which makes it a great place for him to kick off a tour like this that's focused on jobs
and their job.
What do you think about his human touch?
He seems to really connect with people.
He's not afraid to laugh and I think the final question, the veteran with the VA, how
does all that strike you the way he connects with people?
How does he do it?
Well, I'm quite sure that veterans got his issue taken care of by now.
I hope so.
I think it really does come across very clearly that he understands that while we are seeing
some positive trends that there are people that are still out there that are hurting and
people that either don't have a job and are desperate for one or have a job and are
worried about their ability to keep it.
And so that's sort of connected connection comes through very clearly.
He said it himself today and it's hard to imagine when you look at him on stage and say
he's the president of the United States, but it wasn't long ago, six or eight years ago,
he was paying off student loans and trying to figure out which bill to pay.
And to me, that's very, very different than past presidents.
Obviously very different from President Bush who really had to worry much about where
he's built his man.
That kind of common touch and that kind of groundedness is very important.
It comes across, but not only does it come across that way, I think it's genuine and real.
And that's why I'm confident that ultimately we're going to get this back.
Do you think the president will come here to campaign for you next year?
Well, there hasn't been any discussion of that.
I did have the opportunity to meet with him prior to his coming out.
You were at Pulaski.
No, I think it was.
That was a funny faux pas.
Exactly.
But we talked a little bit about the area and some of the channels that were facing.
I let him know that we're thankful for his effort and what he plans to put in place.
As a mayor, there were certainly aspects of the Recovery Act that were important to help
and stabilize our situation from a budgetary standpoint and talk a bit about that.
And briefly talked about the race and he obviously was aware of the fact that I'm running
for Congress.
I think he's looking forward to having another Democratic voice in Congress to help him,
as I said, kind of roll up our seats collectively to get busy, you know, economy moving forward.
He really wanted to hear about how, you know, as a mayor of Bethel and the last six years
taking the largest single-own-of-round field in the United States and making those critical
infrastructure investments, getting that site shovel ready in conjunction with the private
sector and the results that we've had.
And the results are dramatic.
Just on the LVIP site alone, there's over 2,000 jobs at LVIP 7, 1,000 jobs in the associate
with the casino and everybody's felt well aware of that.
And in totality over the last seven years, we've had upwards, or six years, upwards of
about 5,000 new jobs and over 2 billion hours of investment in the city.
And he was pretty impressed by those numbers.
So if Aino, and I think he's looking forward to having someone down in DC who knows
not just the what to do, but kind of the how to get it done.
And I think we need more of that in Washington.
